about.title: About Bond Calculator - Fixed Income Investment Analysis Tool
about.description: The Bond Calculator is a comprehensive fixed income analysis tool designed to help investors evaluate bond investments, calculate yields, and assess bond pricing. Whether you're analyzing government bonds, corporate bonds, or municipal bonds, this calculator provides accurate calculations for current yield, yield to maturity, duration, and bond valuation. Understanding bond calculations is essential for fixed income investing and portfolio management.

faq.q: What's the difference between current yield and yield to maturity?
faq.a: Current yield is the annual coupon payment divided by current market price. Yield to maturity (YTM) considers all cash flows including capital gains/losses if held to maturity. YTM provides a more comprehensive return measure for bond investments.

faq.q: How do interest rates affect bond prices?
faq.a: Bond prices move inversely to interest rates. When rates rise, existing bond prices fall because new bonds offer higher yields. When rates fall, existing bond prices rise. Duration measures this price sensitivity to interest rate changes.

faq.q: Are municipal bonds better than corporate bonds?
faq.a: Municipal bonds offer tax-free income for federal taxes (and sometimes state taxes), making them attractive for high-income investors. Corporate bonds typically offer higher yields but are taxable. Compare after-tax yields to determine which is better for your situation.

faq.q: What is bond duration and why does it matter?
faq.a: Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest rate changes. Higher duration means greater price volatility. It helps investors understand interest rate risk and is crucial for bond portfolio management and hedging strategies.
